source_text: Exposita liberalitate gratiae in hominum salvatorum copia comparat donum atque peccatum et eruditissime ad laudem doni applicat, quod multis vulneribus una virtute medicetur: Et non sicut per unum - inquit - peccatum ita et donum.
pass_a_gloss: The liberality of grace having been explained in the plenty of saved human beings, he compares the gift and sin and most learnedly applies to the praise of the gift that by one virtue it heals many wounds: And not as through one, he says, sin so also the gift.

lemmas.lexica: LS donum; Blaise grace-gift vs inherited sin
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS gratia=favor; Blaise grace; in iustitia definitions often 'favoritism'
LS vulnus; Blaise sin as wound

pass_b_english: Having explained grace’s generosity in the abundance of people saved, he compares the gift and sin. With great learning he praises the gift for healing many wounds by one power: ‘And the gift,’ he says, ‘is not as it was through one sin’ (Romans 5:16).

choices.why: Rom 5 contrast of Adam's offense and Christ's gift; keep gift, not later 'grace system'.
Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: From Pass B Scripture tagging; wording follows Julian's Latin, not a modern Bible.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
